candidates.dedup_key: ast structure aware code chunking versus fixed size and sliding window for retrieval augmented code generation
candidates.title: Chunk on the Syntax Tree, or Don't Bother? What the Benchmarks Say About Code RAG
candidates.summary: Coding assistants and code-RAG systems must split a repository into chunks before they can retrieve from it, and the open question is where to cut. cAST (EMNLP 2025) argues for cutting on the abstract syntax tree so every chunk is a syntactically whole unit, reporting a 4.3-point Recall@5 gain on RepoEval retrieval and a 2.67-point Pass@1 gain on SWE-bench generation over fixed-size chunking. A 2026 controlled study complicates that headline: structure-aware and sliding-window chunking perform comparably, cross-file context budget matters more than the chunking rule, and the one robust finding is that splitting on function boundaries is strictly worse. The piece explains how AST chunking works (tree-sitter as the parsing substrate), what the benchmarks actually measure (RepoEval, from RepoCoder; CodeRAG-Bench), and reaches a calibrated verdict: structure helps, but by less and more conditionally than the single-paper headline implies, and the rule that survives every study is simply do not split mid-function.
candidates.why_relevant: Squarely in the author's domain: this blog's own retrieval avatar chunks prose for a RAG index, and every coding agent chunks code the same way. The topic is technical and mechanism-first (an explainer, not an opinion piece), and unusually it is well-sourced on BOTH sides, so the argument can be honest about the size of the effect instead of selling one paper's headline number.

sources.label: cAST: Enhancing Code RAG with Structural Chunking via Abstract Syntax Tree (Zhang et al., EMNLP 2025 Findings)
sources.excerpt: This approach generates self-contained, semantically coherent units across programming languages and tasks, improving performance on diverse code generation tasks, e.g., boosting Recall@5 by 4.3 points on RepoEval retrieval and Pass@1 by 2.67 points on SWE-bench generation.

sources.label: How Does Chunking Affect Retrieval-Augmented Code Completion? A Controlled Empirical Study (Wu, Gong, Jahangirova, Zhang, 2026)
sources.excerpt: Contrary to intuition, chunking based on functions underperforms all other strategies by 3.57--5.64 percentage points on RepoEval (Cliff's delta = -1.0), while the remaining chunking strategies perform comparably. We also find that cross-file context length is the dominant parameter: doubling from 2,048 to 8,192 tokens yields up to 4.2 percentage points of improvement, whereas chunk size has a weaker, non-monotonic effect. On the cost--quality Pareto front, Sliding Window and cAST dominate both benchmarks; Function chunking is never Pareto-optimal.

sources.label: CodeRAG-Bench: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation? (Wang et al., NAACL 2025 Findings)
sources.excerpt: Notably, GPT-4o shows a 27.4% increase when using gold documents on SWE-bench, indicating that retrieval significantly enhances performance when paired with strong core generation capabilities, even in highly challenging coding tasks. All models show gains of 7.5-17.2 points with canonical snippets in RepoEval.

sources.label: CodeXEmbed: A Generalist Embedding Model Family for Multilingual and Multi-task Code Retrieval (Liu et al.)
sources.excerpt: When averaged over all 10 datasets in the CoIR benchmark, CodeXEmbed7B model achieves the best results, exceeding the SOTA code-domain specific model Voyage-Code-002 by over 20%.

sources.label: Tree-sitter, official documentation (Introduction)
sources.excerpt: Tree-sitter is a parser generator tool and an incremental parsing library. It can build a concrete syntax tree for a source file and efficiently update the syntax tree as the source file is edited.

sources.label: RepoCoder: Repository-Level Code Completion Through Iterative Retrieval and Generation (Zhang et al., EMNLP 2023), origin of RepoEval
sources.excerpt: Experimental results indicate that RepoCoder significantly improves the In-File completion baseline by over 10% in all settings and consistently outperforms the vanilla retrieval-augmented code completion approach.
